correctness.rationale: The reverse-complement identity equates the leading-one run length and binary trailing-zero valuation for every canonical even-length antipalindrome, including the all-ones-first-half case. For an integer quotient, equality/strict inequality of valuations gives exact odd/even mantissa shells. The explicit excluded intervals have exactly counted parity-restricted cardinalities; uniform scale-4 asymptotics attain global minimum \(19/54\) at normalized scale 3/2. A standard-library checker exhaustively corroborates 65,025 ordered small pairs and eight boundary counts; the proof itself handles all lengths and all indices.

evidence: Bai et al. Corollary 19 proves at least \(1/60\) nonrepresentable density for antipalindrome quotients.
Bai et al. Corollary 9 treats ordinary palindromes, a different quotient set, with bound 1/40.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The published \(1/60\) bound does not imply \(19/54\). Its antipalindrome proof restricts a narrow first-three-bit cylinder with residue 1 modulo 4, whereas the new proof excludes full parity-separated power-of-four intervals using equality of initial one-run length and trailing-zero valuation. The ordinary-palindrome result does not dominate the antipalindrome claim.

originality.rationale: The accessible full primary paper arXiv:2202.13694v1, Section 3.4 Theorem 18 and Corollary 19, proves a \(1/60\) nonrepresentability lower-density bound, not the \(19/54\) theorem. Its Conjecture 5 remains stronger. OEIS lists early integer examples but no covering asymptotic. The valuation/shell mechanism improves the published lower bound by more than twentyfold. Extensive relevant external searches and mathematical-research-index searches revealed no covering result; unindexed equivalent work remains possible.

value.rationale: Bai et al. explicitly conjecture zero density for representable antipalindrome quotients. Their established lower bound \(1/60\) for the complement is strengthened to \(19/54\), a factor greater than 21, via a natural structural 2-adic/leading-prefix mechanism and an exact asymptotic obstruction density, rather than a finite table or routine normalization. This is a meaningful quantitative step toward the published problem without claiming to resolve it.
